builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: The Precision Wall: An Optimizer-Dependent Boundary for Optimization under Power-Law Measurement Spectra
summary: The paper does not propose a deployable technique; it replaces trial-and-error diagnosis of first-order optimizer stalls in low-rank matrix sensing with a closed-form boundary predicting when denominator-normalized optimizers (e.g., Adam) hit a numerical precision wall under power-law measurement spectra. Adopting the finding costs nothing computationally but applies only to a narrow sensing setting with heavy-tailed covariance, and the approximation already fails at D = 2, exhibits a finite-D spectral crossover, and saturates below epsilon = 1e-8 at a dynamical floor. For standard LLM training or inference on a single 24 GB GPU, the result offers no actionable gain, since its predictions concern a specific optimization landscape rather than model quality or efficiency.
rationale: This is a diagnostic analysis of optimizer failure in low-rank matrix sensing, not a method the reader can deploy, so it is worth monitoring only if their workloads involve similar heavy-tailed optimization landscapes.
technique: Precision-wall boundary formula for optimizer selection

claims.statement: The paper does not propose a deployable technique; it replaces trial-and-error diagnosis of first-order optimizer stalls in low-rank matrix sensing with a closed-form boundary predicting when denominator-normalized optimizers (e.g., Adam) hit a numerical precision wall under power-law measurement spectra. Adopting the finding costs nothing computationally but applies only to a narrow sensing setting with heavy-tailed covariance, and the approximation already fails at D = 2, exhibits a finite-D spectral crossover, and saturates below epsilon = 1e-8 at a dynamical floor. For standard LLM training or inference on a single 24 GB GPU, the result offers no actionable gain, since its predictions concern a specific optimization landscape rather than model quality or efficiency.
With a frozen calibrated lag, the closed-form boundary predicts Adam's stall onset within 0.45 in the exponent across all 16 held-out configurations of the (V, D) grid.
